news.title: EFL Trophy holders Luton face Palace U21s in last 32
news.summary: Jersey Mike's signed a five-year sponsorship deal with the EFL in September
body: Jersey Mike's signed a five-year sponsorship deal with the EFL in September
Holders Luton Town will host Crystal Palace Under-21s in the last 32 of the Jersey Mike's Trophy.
The Hatters, who beat Stockport County 3-1 in last season's EFL Trophy final at Wembley, won their group in the opening stages of the competition, coming through their three matches unbeaten.
Three-time winners Peterborough United have been drawn away at Plymouth Argyle with Posh hoping to win the trophy for a record fourth time.
Wycombe Wanderers have been handed a potentially attractive tie at home to Arsenal's U21s while Leicester City visit Barnet.

In the northern section, last year's runners-up Stockport will face League Two strugglers Port Vale while Wigan Athletic and Doncaster Rovers, who have both won the competition twice will meet at The Brick Community Stadium.
Managerless Blackpool, who have also won the trophy on two previous occasions have been drawn away at Notts County.

news.title: Leicester no longer for sale as owner refocuses on future
news.summary: King Power, the Thai business that Khun Aiyawatt 'Top' Srivaddhanaprabha is part of, bought Leicester for £35m in 2010
body: King Power, the Thai business that Khun Aiyawatt 'Top' Srivaddhanaprabha is part of, bought Leicester for £35m in 2010

Leicester City owner Khun Aiyawatt 'Top' Srivaddhanaprabha has confirmed the one-time Premier League title winners are no longer up for sale and there will be a "refocus" on rebuilding the side after years of decline.

The Foxes were put on the market in the summer after back-to-back relegations saw the side drop from the Premier League and straight through the Championship to land in England's third tier for just the second time in the club's 142-year history.

A sales brochure was produced by US investment bank Citigroup in which an asking price of more than £200m was put on a League One club that a decade ago had defied all expectations by winning the Premier League title at 5,000-1 odds.

Leicester never publicly acknowledged that the club had been put up for sale, with under-fire chief football officer Jon Rudkin going so far as to say he "cannot comment on speculation" when asked about it in a rare interview with BBC Radio Leicester in October.

Khun Top, however, has now said that there were no takers when investment had been sought for a side that the Srivaddhanaprabha family, through its King Power duty free business in Thailand, have owned for 16 years.

"We recently undertook a structured process to explore whether new investment or a change of ownership could actually be the right thing for the club," Khun Top wrote in an open letter to Leicester City supporters on the club's website., external
"Those discussions have not resulted in an agreement, and I have decided to conclude the process to enable us to refocus on the work needed to move the club forward."
'Business as always' - Foxes boss Martin brushes off sales talk
Follow Leicester City on BBC Sounds
Pre-match, post-match and topical Foxes content

Three relegations in four years, having yo-yoed between the Premier League and Championship before going down to League One, has badly damaged the relationship between the Foxes' owners and their supporter base.

While a golden age of success was bankrolled by King Power, with Premier League glory in 2016 followed up by FA Cup success in 2021, high spending on an underperforming side in recent years has led to an increasing number of supporters calling for Khun Top to sell up.
But the Thai businessman said he has a "deep connection" to Leicester and "its people".

And it is not just euphoric sporting moments that have forged the bond he is talking about, as his father - and predecessor as Foxes chairman - Khun Vichai died in a helicopter crash outside the stadium in 2018.
"For my family and me, Leicester City has been a big part of our lives for many years," he said.
"We have experienced extraordinary moments together, as well as some very difficult ones."
Khun Top added that the struggles of recent years, which included the club being hit with a points penalty last season for breaking spending rules, has got him "thinking a lot about our direction".
Earlier this year he told BBC Radio Leicester that he shoulders the blame for the club's decline.
"Making better decisions" as well as "continuing to learn from our past experiences" are two steps the club "need to take", he said.
Khun Top has insisted that through King Power, a company that has endured difficulties in recent years, the club's "financial position remains secure".
However, he added that there was "work needed to put Leicester City on a more sustainable footing".

"That has been a principle behind the work and decisions of the last year – giving the club the appropriate support for its immediate circumstances, while building the organisational discipline and financial resilience that will underpin a responsible plan for future growth," he said.
As part of Khun Top's missive, he confirmed that chief executive Kevin Davies will be stepping down from the role in December.
Davies had only been in the job since March, and was promoted to the position after a shake-up of a number of leadership roles.

news.title: 'Most frustrating of career' - Martin on Foxes draw at Blackpool
news.summary: This video can not be played
body: This video can not be played
'We should win. You know that, I know that'
A squandered victory at the seaside has redefined Russell Martin's definition of frustration.

The Leicester City manager said he was "hurt" by the solitary point his side picked up in Tuesday's 1-1 draw at lowly Blackpool in League One after dominating just about every facet of the game – controlling 77% possession and amassing 30 shots, of which nine were on target.
Asked if the draw was the most frustrating moment of the season, former Rangers and Southampton boss Martin replied by saying: "This season? Of my short but feels like very long managerial career."

That says a lot coming from a manager who was smuggled out of the stadium under police escort then sacked at Rangers after a draw with Falkirk last season, and whose Southampton side was once undone in the Premier League by two second-half Mohamed Salah goals after leading 2-1.

Those were tenure-defining defeats for a manager whose reputation has taken a battering in recent seasons, with his style of possession-heavy, passing football – an approach he once said was to "dominate the ball and be aggressive with it", external – coming in for particular ridicule when results have gone against his side.

It has been the same at one-time Premier League title winners Leicester this season in the third tier, with Martin's method called into question in the early months of his tenure after the Foxes got off to a slow start.
Results have improved in recent weeks - they are unbeaten in six matches across all competitions and are up to seventh in the table.
But victory would have had them within a point of the play-off places, and Martin said the result will leave him "eternally frustrated".
"We should win, I know that, you know that and I think everyone in the stadium knows that. But we don't," he told BBC Radio Leicester after the match at Bloomfield Road.
"How we only score one goal, I'm really struggling to come to terms with.
"We have brilliant chances in the middle of their goal, not like half chances. And we actually score a goal that is really brilliant, but we shouldn't need a goal like that to win the game.
"I'm not frustrated, I'm hurt that we don't win the game and we concede a rubbish goal."
Blackpool 1-1 Leicester City

It took more than an hour for the Foxes to break Blackpool's resistance, with a deluge of chances missed before Will Alves cut in from the left to beat home goalkeeper Bailey Peacock-Farrell with a shot that took a slight deflection.
It was six minutes from the end when Niall Ennis scrambled home the leveller for the Seasiders.
"I'm really proud of the players and how much they have grown in terms of what the performances look like," said Martin.
"But it's my job to be demanding of them, and there is no way we should be drawing that game. No way."
